leading.$description: Screen runs looser than paper. Everything below title clears the Korean 1.5 floor; title and above answer to the display floor of 1.2 instead, because forcing 1.5 onto a 96px Hangul line is a setting error, not compliance.

rule-rhythm.$description: Where a blank sits under the word it holds. Offset is measured from the text baseline box, and the thickness comes from border.rule — if these drift the rule stops reading as a printed line and starts reading as an underline decoration.

measure.$description: 65–75ch is the readability band; prose sits inside it and claim is deliberately short because a claim is not prose.

gutter-narrow.$description: phone. Desk-scale padding eats a 375 viewport.

content.$description: cap for list-shaped content, so a trailing count column still associates with its row

breakpoint.$description: Media queries cannot read custom properties, so these are the ONE place a px literal is allowed outside the token files, and only at a value declared here. check-tokens.mjs enforces that. A breakpoint can never be a runtime token in any tool — Tailwind's @theme emits invalid CSS and fails the build outright.

leading.$description: Paper runs tighter than screen at the same apparent size — ink on stock needs less air than backlit glass. Body stays above the Korean 1.5 floor.

read.$description: 명조 body. The interior is set in this and nothing else.

rule-rhythm.$description: On paper the blank is not a mark under a word, it is a place to write. Pitch and height are what make that true; a rule set to web values leaves a line nobody can write on.

write-height.$description: clear vertical room above the rule. This is the interior's whole argument: if it is not there, the page is a picture of a form rather than a form.

tracking.$description: Print tracks marginally wider than screen: no subpixel rendering to hold the counters open, and ink spreads into the stock.

prose.$description: narrower than web — an A4 column is fixed and the web measure overruns it at print body size

frame.$description: Page geometry has no web counterpart. These are medium-specific rather than forked, which ENGINE §2.1 allows explicitly.

margin-inner.$description: gutter side, wider — the binding eats it

margin-outer.$description: outer margin is NOT trimmed to fit more text: it is where the reader's hand rests and where notes go
